section_summary: This section discusses financing Japan’s economic recovery, including a proposed rehabilitation appropriation, cotton import credit, and prewar foreign debts. It also contains Chinese editorial objections to the American recovery plan, a Japanese coalition policy agreement, correspondence about banks’ participation in cotton loans, and a despatch on the sale of securities by liquidation agencies. A lengthy securities sales table begins on page 495 and continues beyond this section.

subfiles.title: Economic Rehabilitation Occupied Areas (EROA) Estimate for Japan
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, Acting Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The Political Adviser questions a separate $180 million rehabilitation appropriation for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Sebald argues that some proposed EROA purchases might instead be covered by GARIOA, with other needs financed through available credits, barter, and occupation funds. He cites likely congressional difficulties and adverse Asian reactions to a labelled rehabilitation program, while acknowledging that a larger recovery program might require a separate appropriation.

subfiles.title: We Oppose the U.S. Plan for Rehabilitating the Japanese Economy
subfiles.about: A Chinese editorial opposes American financing of Japanese industrial recovery.
subfiles.summary: The editorial argues that U.S. investment would make Japan dependent on American capital while restoring its industrial dominance in Asia. It predicts resistance to Japanese goods and urges China to reject the plan.

subfiles.title: We Refute the View That Japan Should Be Made the Factory of Asia
subfiles.about: A Chinese editorial rejects proposals to make Japan an industrial center for Asia.
subfiles.summary: The editorial contends that the American recovery plan would benefit the United States while harming China and other Asian countries.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning EROA estimate for Japan
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltz, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department answers Sebald’s objections to a separate Japanese rehabilitation appropriation.
subfiles.summary: The Department says other Far Eastern Commission members have already been informed of the U.S. self-support policy for Japan. It considers a distinct rehabilitation request more persuasive to Congress, while declining to commit to a fixed schedule for future aid reductions.

subfiles.title: Japan’s Foreign Obligations
subfiles.about: The article assesses Japan’s prewar foreign loans and their possible postwar repayment.
subfiles.summary: It tabulates outstanding principal and interest, explains wartime yen payments into a custody account, and warns that exchange rate changes would greatly increase the yen cost of repayment. It urges careful settlement to preserve Japan’s credit standing.

subfiles.title: Proposed Cotton Credit for Japan
subfiles.about: The memorandum reviews a proposed $60 million credit for American cotton imports into Japan.
subfiles.summary: Whitman describes participation by the Export-Import Bank and private banks, repayment from exports, and security in Japanese precious metals. He recommends prompt support while noting demanding collateral terms and proposing changes to the loan agreement.

subfiles.title: Policy Agreement Reached by the Democratic, Social-Democratic, and People’s Cooperative Parties
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Sebald forwards the Japanese coalition parties’ policy agreement and an abstract.
subfiles.summary: He says the broad agreement enabled Prime Minister Ashida to form a cabinet but left disputes over war bond interest, banking reform, nationalization, taxation, and agrarian reform unresolved.

subfiles.title: Abstract of the Official Tripartite Policy Agreement
subfiles.from: Government Section, Parliamentary and Political Division
subfiles.about: The abstract lists the coalition parties’ political, economic, production, and social proposals.
subfiles.summary: It outlines tax and banking changes, production expansion, possible state control of industries, agricultural reform, housing, and unemployment relief.

subfiles.title: Text of the Tripartite Policy Agreement
subfiles.from: Democratic, Social Democratic, and People’s Cooperative parties
subfiles.about: The agreement sets out the proposed policies of Japan’s new governing coalition.
subfiles.summary: The parties propose a two-year production plan, anti-inflation measures, tax and banking reform, and selective state management of key industries. The agreement also addresses labor, agriculture, housing, repatriation, and unemployment.

subfiles.title: Small-bank participation in cotton loans to Japan
subfiles.to: George C. Marshall, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: DuBois asks that smaller banks have opportunities to participate in proposed cotton loans to Japan.
subfiles.summary: He questions why the reported loan is concentrated among a few large banks and suggests inviting smaller banks to participate.

subfiles.title: Forwarding cotton-loan correspondence to the Department of the Army
subfiles.from: Edward W. Doherty, Division of Financial Affairs
subfiles.to: Paul Cleveland, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Doherty forwards correspondence about small-bank participation in proposed Japanese cotton loans.
subfiles.summary: He sends the bankers’ letter and the Department’s reply to Cleveland.

subfiles.title: Forwarding cotton-loan correspondence to the Export-Import Bank
subfiles.about: The Department forwards the bankers’ inquiry for a more informed response.
subfiles.summary: The transmittal says the Export-Import Bank is better placed to answer questions about participation in the cotton loan.

subfiles.title: Reply to Ben DuBois concerning cotton loans
subfiles.from: Edward W. Doherty, for the Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department directs DuBois’s bank-participation inquiry to the lenders.
subfiles.summary: Doherty refers the inquiry to the Export-Import Bank and participating private banks.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement for Tokyo despatch no. 213
subfiles.about: The form identifies a replacement record copy of despatch no. 213.
subfiles.summary: A copy replaces the unreturned original action copy.

subfiles.title: Sale of Securities Through Liquidation Agencies
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Sebald reports progress and risks in Japanese government liquidation agencies’ securities sales.
subfiles.summary: The despatch describes sales by the CILC, HCLC, and SCLC and reports shares sold and securities still held. Sebald warns that public-tender sales make ultimate ownership difficult to trace and could allow a new wealthy group to acquire concentrated economic control.

subfiles.title: Report of Securities Disposed
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The enclosure tabulates securities offered and sold by Japanese liquidation agencies.
subfiles.summary: The table records issuing companies, offering agencies, locations, intended buyers, sale dates, numbers of shares, prices, and proceeds. It covers transactions from July 1947 through February 1948. The table continues beyond page 544.
